name: ioprio_get
synopsis: int syscall(SYS_ioprio_get, int which, int who);
description: The ioprio_get() system call retrieves the I/O scheduling class and priority of one or more threads based on the specified criteria. It identifies threads using the 'which' and 'who' arguments, and returns the highest priority among matching processes.

parameters.name: which
parameters.description: Determines how the 'who' argument is interpreted, such as IOPRIO_WHO_PROCESS, IOPRIO_WHO_PGRP, or IOPRIO_WHO_USER.

parameters.name: who
parameters.description: Identifies the thread(s) to operate on, such as a process ID, process group ID, or user ID.

return_value.success: Returns the ioprio value of the process with the highest I/O priority among the matching processes.
return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set to indicate the error.

errors.description: Invalid value for which or ioprio.
The calling process does not have the necessary privileges.

bugs: glibc does not yet provide a suitable header file defining the function prototypes and macros described on this page. Suitable definitions can be found in linux/ioprio.h.
